summary: The audit checks 90 units of graduate coursework, counting at most 18 units of ME 400 thesis work. Checked by hand: the Engineer thesis, 21 units of approved 200-level math, science and engineering courses beyond the MS (no research, directed study, seminars or practical training), finishing the Stanford MS requirements, and faculty approval with a 3.0 GPA in courses beyond the master's.

add.why: "In addition to the thesis, 21 units of approved course work in mathematics, science and engineering (excluding research, directed study, seminars, curricular practical training, and course) are required" "these 21 units must be beyond the 45-unit master's coursework. These courses must be numbered 200+, and must be taken for a letter grade, and have primarily technical content." "The choice of courses is subject to the advisor's approval." The fields name no subject codes, so the student moves the courses in.
"Students who have not fulfilled the Stanford MS degree requirements must do so, with allowance for approximate equivalence of courses taken elsewhere; up to 45 units may be transferable."

add.why: "Candidates for the degree must have faculty approval and have a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 for all courses (exclusive of thesis credit and other independent study courses) taken beyond those required for the master's degree."
